Drax, Brookfield and Radiant, Brookfield’s UK-headquartered AI infrastructure platform, have announced a new strategic partnership to jointly develop, deliver and operate GW-scale data centre capacity at Drax Power Station in North Yorkshire.

The Brookfield-Qai AI infrastructure joint venture will provide backing for the project. Brookfield estimates that total investment in the development could potentially exceed £20bn, including an initial £2.5bn as part of the first phase.

Drax Power Station is at the heart of UK energy security and has supported the country’s growth for over 50 years, powering millions of homes and businesses and employing generations of local workers. This new partnership aligns to the Government’s AI sovereignty and reindustrialisation ambitions. It represents the next chapter in the site’s role meeting national electricity demand and supporting Yorkshire and the UK’s economies and it can help deliver a long-term future for the power station.

The companies are planning to develop data centre capacity on site in phases: Phase 1: targeting up to 100MW, operational from Q1 2028; Phase 2: ambition to ramp up to 500MW of capacity between 2028 and 2031; and Phase 3: ambition to develop additional capacity post 2031.

Progression of the first phase is subject to the timely progression of the necessary planning, as well as receiving the required regulatory and network approvals from Government and the system operator, in addition to securing a suitable tenant for the project.

The power station estate comprises 1,000 acres and 4GW of grid access, with 2.6GW of active dispatchable generation and cooling systems. The site also benefits from its proximity to the UK fibre network, making it ideal for faster and more certain development of data centres.

The UK Government is clear that countries able to host and power data centres will be better placed to protect their sovereignty, strengthen economic resilience, capture the benefits of the digital economy and shape the future of AI.

The companies welcome the Government’s new Data Centre Covenant and its pathway to accelerate time to power and planning for strategically important data centres. The companies’ initial assessment is that this project aligns with the Covenant’s criteria, supporting energy security, delivering local community benefits, meeting environmental standards, enabling reindustrialisation and strengthening the UK’s access to secure infrastructure.

As part of their shared commitment to delivering lasting local benefits, the partners expect to establish a voluntary community benefits fund, developed in consultation with communities around the Drax Power Station site, that is separate from and additional to any planning obligations and Drax’s existing community initiatives. A community consultation on the plans will begin shortly with the formal planning process following afterward.

Drax Group CEO, Will Gardiner, said: “We are proud to be partnering with leading AI infrastructure providers on this project which can help secure the long-term future of the site and protect hundreds of jobs, maintain a critical source of this country’s energy security, support northern growth and enable us to continue delivering for our local communities.

“This country has a unique opportunity to bring together AI leadership, energy infrastructure and industrial renewal to drive national growth. If constructed in full, this project could become one of the largest data centres in the UK, attracting billions in inward investment, supporting the North’s reindustrialisation and strengthening sovereign AI capability.”

Brookfield Head of AI infrastructure, Sikander Rashid, said: “Teaming up with Drax and Qai for this project represents a major opportunity for our AI infrastructure strategy. Our capital and deep operating capabilities will help accelerate the construction of a critical piece of sovereign AI, delivered by Radiant, our UK-headquartered compute infrastructure platform. In addition to preserving hundreds of jobs, this project will also create many direct and indirect jobs around the broader Yorkshire area.”

Radiant CEO, Mahdi Yahya, said: “We are proud to expand our UK AI compute footprint with Drax. This is a unique opportunity for the UK’s AI ecosystem to build at scale. By designing, building and operating from the UK, it will give British researchers, startups and enterprises access to frontier compute at home. Drax has powered Britain for more than fifty years. Together we can power its AI economy for the next fifty.”

Qai Chairman and Managing Director, Abdulla Al-Misnad, said: “This project is a major initiative under the Brookfield-Qai joint venture and forms part of our international AI infrastructure strategy. Drawing on the combined expertise of Qai and Brookfield in developing and managing large-scale critical infrastructure, and with Radiant and Drax delivering the project, we are helping to establish the infrastructure required to support the long-term growth of the UK’s AI ecosystem.”

# Drax 携手 Brookfield、卡塔尔 Qai 拟建吉瓦级 AI 数据中心：潜在总投资超 200 亿英镑

英国能源企业 Drax 11 月 3 日官宣：与 Brookfield、其英国 AI 基础设施平台 Radiant 及卡塔尔 Qai 达成战略合作，在北约克郡 Drax 电站园区分阶段建设吉瓦级 AI 数据中心。潜在总投资（含芯片）可超 200 亿英镑（约 268 亿美元），首期 25 亿英镑、最高 100MW、目标 2028 年一季度投运，2028–2031 年扩至 500MW，2031 年后迈向超 1GW。园区坐拥 4GW 电网接入与 2.6GW 可调度发电，是欧洲主权 AI 基建的代表性落子，首期仍取决于规划许可与承租客户。

## 事件：官方新闻稿与上市公司公告同日披露

11 月 3 日，英国能源企业 Drax 与 Brookfield 及其总部位于英国的 AI 基础设施平台 Radiant 宣布达成战略合作，联合开发、交付并运营位于北约克郡 Drax 电站园区的吉瓦级数据中心容量，资金由 Brookfield 与卡塔尔 Qai 于 2025 年成立的 AI 基础设施合资平台提供。Drax 同日发布上市公司 RNS 公告。Brookfield 估算，包含半导体芯片在内，项目全周期潜在总投资可超 200 亿英镑（新浪财经折算约 268 亿美元），其中首期投资约 25 亿英镑。消息公布当日，Drax 伦敦上市股票早盘上涨——新浪财经口径为 8.2%，优分析口径为约 9%，两家转述略有出入。

分阶段规划：一期目标最高 100MW，计划 2028 年一季度投运；二期计划 2028 至 2031 年间将容量提升至 500MW，届时可利用电站现有机组通过长期购电协议直接供应全天候电力；三期目标在 2031 年后继续扩建，最终在该地块实现超 1GW 总容量。Drax 与英国政府的差价合约允许其申请将最多 500MW 容量用于数据中心，但仍需政府及相关机构同意。

## 为什么重要：欧洲主权 AI 基建的样板项目

这个项目的看点不在单一投资额，而在三件事叠加：其一，规模——首期即 25 亿英镑、终局超 1GW，一旦建成将成为英国最大的数据中心之一；其二，选址逻辑——园区拥有 1000 英亩土地、4GW 电网接入容量、2.6GW 可调度发电与配套冷却系统，且邻近英国光纤骨干网，是英国少数能向数据中心客户直接供应大规模可靠电力的场地，把「能源基础设施 + AI 算力」拧在同一个项目里；其三，资本结构——Brookfield（全球另类资产管理巨头）与卡塔尔 Qai（多哈投资平台旗下科技企业）的合资平台出资，英国政府财政大臣首席秘书 Emma Reynolds 与科学、创新与投资大臣 Chris McDonald 均在官方稿中背书，后者明确将这一定位为「来自卡塔尔和 Brookfield 的投资」与英卡伙伴关系的注脚。

项目方同时表示欢迎英国政府新推出的数据中心契约（Data Centre Covenant），并认为自身规划与其关键标准吻合——该契约旨在为战略性数据中心加速电力接入与规划审批。Radiant CEO Mahdi Yahya 的表述是让「英国研究者、初创企业与企业在本土获得前沿算力」。

## 前提与风险：一切取决于许可、客户与最终投资决定

官方稿明确：一期推进取决于规划审批的及时进展、获得政府与系统运营商所需的监管及电网批准，以及为项目敲定合适承租客户，最终投资决定尚待各方作出。一期电力将直接取自电网而非 Drax 机组专供；公司正准备一期规划申请，公众咨询即将启动。摩根大通分析师认为 Brookfield 的加入有助于提高市场对项目落地的信心，也可能强化电站在 2031 年 3 月补贴方案到期后持续运营的预期，但实际规模与收益仍取决于客户承诺、核准进度与分期投资决策。换言之，200 亿英镑是「潜在」口径，落地节奏存在不确定性。
